newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: U.S. forest investment imminent - NZ Herald.
newsitem.headline: U.S. forest investment imminent - NZ Herald.

text.p: A Boston company will soon announce plans to invest around US$100 million in New Zealand forestry, the New Zealand Herald said on Monday.
The Herald, quoting Kelly Beeman, director of the North America Investment promotion unit, said the transaction was imminent and certain.
The unit works from the New Zealand consulate-general in Los Angeles.

The Herald said Beeman and Ministry of Forestry officials recently toured seven U.S. cities and Vancouver to encourage North American timber interests to link forest resources in New Zealand with wood product manufacturers.
"New Zealand is rightly viewed as the most stable and efficient producer of trees, especially of radiata pine, in the world," Beeman said.
But North Anmerican mills were far larger and more efficient than their New Zealand counterparts, and U.S. investors could improve New Zealand's technology and access to markets.
Beeman said a key to the development of New Zealand's forest potential was a system of brokerage between small wood lot owners and mills needing steady supply of timber.
